title: Teach the solver the planning rules

blocks.text: A colleague wrote the selection model below with the budget and nothing else, and the solver now funds a breaker bay without the tower it sits on. The planning rules live in the `Project` records: `must_do`, `parent` and `group` (projects sharing a group are alternatives, as in the lesson's repair-or-replace pair).

Write `add_rules(model, x, projects)` in `selection.py`, adding one linear constraint per rule to the MathOpt model. `x[pid]` is the binary variable for project `pid`. `build_model` and `solve` already call it; the tests build the model, fix a plan by its variables' bounds, and ask the solver whether that plan is allowed.
The model to implement, with $`P`$ the projects, $`M`$ the must-do ones, $`C`$ the ones with a parent $`p(c)`$, and $`\mathcal{G}`$ the groups (each the set of projects sharing a `group`):

\begin{aligned}
\max \;& \sum_{i \in P} \text{value}_i\, x_i \\
\text{s.t. }& \sum_{i \in P} \text{cost}_i\, x_i \le B && && \text{(budget, already written)} \\
& x_i = 1 && \forall i \in M && \text{(must}_i) \\
& x_c \le x_{p(c)} && \forall c \in C && \text{(parent}_c) \\
& \sum_{i \in g} x_i \le 1 && \forall g \in \mathcal{G} && \text{(alt}_g) \\
& x_i \in \{0, 1\} && \forall i \in P
\end{aligned}
`add_rules` adds the three labeled families of rows.

from selection import Project, solve

# Six depot upgrades; D1 is ordered by the inspector.
depots = [
    Project("D1", 30, 45, must_do=True),
    Project("D2", 20, 30),
    Project("D3", 10, 35, parent="D2"),
    Project("D4", 25, 33, group="roof"),
    Project("D5", 15, 26, group="roof"),
    Project("D6", 35, 30),
]

for budget in (120, 80, 40):
    value, plan = solve(depots, budget)
    print(f"budget {budget}:", round(value), sorted(plan))

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Project:
    pid: str
    cost: int
    value: int
    must_do: bool = False
    parent: str | None = None
    group: str | None = None


def add_rules(model: mathopt.Model, x: dict, projects: list[Project]) -> None:
    """Add the must-do, parent-child and alternative rules as linear constraints."""
    # TODO: one linear constraint per rule, written with the variables in x.
    return None


def build_model(projects: list[Project], budget: int) -> tuple[mathopt.Model, dict]:
    model = mathopt.Model(name="selection")
    x = {p.pid: model.add_binary_variable(name=f"x_{p.pid}") for p in projects}
    model.add_linear_constraint(sum(p.cost * x[p.pid] for p in projects) <= budget, name="budget")
    add_rules(model, x, projects)
    model.maximize(sum(p.value * x[p.pid] for p in projects))
    return model, x


def solve(projects: list[Project], budget: int) -> tuple[float, frozenset[str]]:
    model, x = build_model(projects, budget)
    result = mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS)
    return result.objective_value(), frozenset(pid for pid, v in x.items() if result.variable_values(v) > 0.5)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    demo = [Project("A", 50, 80, must_do=True), Project("B", 30, 40), Project("C", 20, 35, parent="B")]
    print(solve(demo, 90))

cases.says: the solver's plan is the most valuable plan the rules allow
a plan without a must-do project is refused, and one with it is allowed
a child alone is refused, and a parent alone is allowed
funding neither alternative is allowed, and funding both is refused

concepts: the yes/no planning rules become linear constraints on binary variables, and a MILP solver then finds the best allowed plan
